# Would adding more class time for programming in python be effecient for student learning?
### Alena Vo and Ashley Nowak


The goal of this analysis was to determine if increasing the amount of class time for active Python coding would improve student learning. Specifically, we examined the data provided for overall programming assignment effectiveness and the hours students spent online. We wanted to see if there was any correlation among the two variables. Additionally, we looked at the data on a broader scale, seeing how COMP110 students rated the overall effectiveness of programming assignments.

## Conclusion 

According to our data, students who spent more time doing online work felt that programming assignments were less effective in learning course content than students who spent less time online. Despite these numbers, the overall majority of COMP110 students felt that programming assignments were effective in learning course content. Over 200 students rated programming effectiveness a 6 or 7 out of 7. With this said, I conclude that spending more time on programming in class will be an effective way to improve learning. I hypothesize that spending more class time on Python coding would lessen the amount of time students spend online as this extra coding time in class would provide students more practice and instructor help. 

In adopting this idea, we run the risk of not having enough class time to go through class slides and memory diagrams. Class slides, memory diagrams, and code writing are all equally important, so managing the time to still give each aspect its proper time may be a challenge. A solution might be adopting a hybrid style classroom. Students could watch pre-lecture videos and spend the first half of class working on related memory diagrams or general course content. Then, students could spend the rest of class practicing code writing on Python. 

Before implementation of this method, it would be important to analyze the data provided from the survey, specifically regarding whether students would like pre-class lecture videos. Furthermore, to extend on this idea, another survey could be taken, gaining knowledge about why some students felt programming assignments were ineffective in learning course content.
